subject: Strategic shift: proposed team role matrix & QBR talking points
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Strategic shift: proposed team role matrix & QBR talking points

Team —

As discussed in last week's leadership forum, I'm proposing we move from a capacity-centric org to a capability-centric structure ahead of the QBR. The attached role matrix (org-role_matrix_v2.xlsx) maps current roles into three cross-cutting squads: Platform (serving/runtime), Product (APIs & UX), and Customer Reliability (SRE + CS ops). The goals: tighter ownership of latency/cost SLOs, clearer rollout ownership for Dedicated/Private deployments, and faster decision cycles for model onboarding.

Key changes I want feedback on by Friday:
- Formal squad leads and escalation paths for infra/perf regressions.
- Which engineering managers should be realigned vs. remain dotted-line.
- Any compliance or customer-risk blockers for the Private rollout.

I've also started a QBR deck draft (qbr-deck-draft.pdf) with the narrative: why we're shifting, impact on OKRs (throughput, cost/unit, SLA attainment), and sample customer-facing messaging. Please review both artifacts in the Drive link below and add comments inline.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cROLEMATRIX
Jira ops ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-1427

Ask: read the matrix and the deck, leave feedback, and tell me if you have hard objections to any of the proposed lead assignments. If no hard objections, we'll surface this in Thursday's executive readout and ask for final approval in the QBR.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Chief Product Officer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: org-role_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 240KB); qbr-deck-draft.pdf (slide deck, 3MB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Strategic shift: proposed team role matrix & QBR talking points

Jonas —

Thanks for the draft. Quick thoughts after a pass through the matrix and slides:

- Platform squad: +1 to making this a single engineering manager90owned area. Suggest we name someone provisional (I nominate Diego or Karthik) so we can communicate a point-of-contact.
- Product squad: the proposed split of API vs. Console makes sense, but Product needs a clear owner for rollout orchestration (model pinning, compatibility testing).
- Customer Reliability: we should explicitize the handover steps for Dedicated customers (runbooks + SLA commitments).

I've added inline comments on the Drive doc. I'm also copying Mark Jensen from Acme Cloud on one item: their marketplace procurement timeline may affect Dedicated go-live windows. Mark: can you flag any constraints on May/June migrations?

Minor: slide 6 on the deck has a cost/unit graph that uses pre-quantization numbers. That projection needs re-run after the quantization recommendation from Optimize.

No hard objections on the leads as currently mapped; I do want to ensure we have a transition plan for any managers who won't move into a new lead role.

-Marissa
VP, Platform Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

Subject: Re: Strategic shift: proposed team role matrix & QBR talking points

Thanks both —

Read the matrix and left a few redlines. A couple items to call out for the QBR:

1) People impact: estimated reorg headcount movement is 12 engineers and 3 managers. We need a clear FAQ for affected individuals (timelines, reporting changes, compensation questions). I'd like Talent to have a draft comms plan by EOD Friday.

2) OKR alignment: we should add an explicit OKR that ties Platform improvements to a measurable unit-cost target (e.g., reduce host token cost by 18% in Q3) so we can track the economic impact of the restructure.

3) Customer escalations: recommend we pre-authorize a limited credits policy for customers affected by migration-related regressions. I'll work with Finance to scope the amount.

I'll be live in the exec readout Thursday and can present the people & risk slide.

-Laura
Head of People Operations
Redwood Inference

Jonas / team —

Appreciate the clear framing. A few logistical items and next steps:

- I've updated the Ops ticket (OPS-1427) with an initial timeline — milestone draft attached to the ticket. Link above.
- I'll own the migration playbook for Dedicated customers and will pair with Marissa on the rollout orchestration owner.
- Laura: we'll sync with Talent on Friday to align the comms timeline; please send the FAQ draft to me and I'll validate wording for impact/risk.

For the QBR: propose a two-slide story arc — (1) why the shift (problem statement + evidence), (2) what success looks like (metrics + transition guardrails). I'll slot 8 minutes in the exec readout for this.

Calendar: I've scheduled a 30-minute QBR prep on Friday 10:00-10:30 PT. Invite: https://calendar.redwood.com/event/abcd1234

If there are no objections by end of business Friday, we'll mark the matrix as 'exec-reviewed' and proceed to external comms prep next week.

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Operations & Reliability
